page: Vultr vhf-2c-4gb is an entry-tier virtual server belonging to the High Frequency Compute family. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it is powered by an Intel processor clocked at 2.0 GHz with 1 physical core presenting 2 virtual CPUs via hyper-threading under a shared CPU allocation model. The system configuration integrates 4.0 GB of system memory (2.0 GB per core), 128 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and one complimentary public IPv4 address. There are no GPUs equipped on this instance.

Hardware instruction features include support for AVX, AES, BMI2, and FMA, while extended instruction sets like AVX-512, AMX, and SHA-NI are unsupported. CPU cache allocations consist of 32 KB L1 data cache, 4 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache. In benchmark evaluations, single-threaded throughput shows varied behavior: gzip compression ranks in the top 25% at 32.63 GB/sec, and stress-ng single-core performance registers within the middle 50% at 1873.78. Conversely, multi-threaded metrics reflect the constrained physical core count, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 1910.0 and a multi-core stress-ng rating of 3596.49 placing in the bottom quartile. Memory bandwidth also shows lower-tier results, reaching 22.81 GB/sec read and 12.89 GB/sec write on large 256 MB blocks.

With its shared single-core hyper-threaded architecture, the instance presents an economical entry point for lightweight compute tasks where resource contention can be tolerated. Its bundled 128 GB NVMe SSD provides solid local storage density relative to its memory size, making it suitable for development environments, low-traffic web serving (3.38 GB/sec in throughput tests), staging environments, and basic caching nodes handling moderate operational volumes such as Redis workloads.
description: Vultr vhf-2c-4gb is a High Frequency Compute instance powered by an Intel x86_64 processor clocked at 2.0 GHz, offering 2 shared vCPUs derived from 1 physical hyper-threaded core. The configuration includes 4.0 GB of RAM, a 128 GB local NVMe SSD, and 1 complimentary public IPv4 address, without discrete GPU hardware. Instruction support covers AVX, AES, and FMA, backed by 16 MB of L3 cache. Benchmark testing highlights solid single-threaded data compression, reaching 32.63 GB/sec in gzip, while multi-core compute and memory bandwidth reflect its entry-level shared profile, scoring 1910.0 in Geekbench multi-core and registering 22.81 GB/sec on uncached memory reads. Given its bundled NVMe capacity and shared execution footprint, the instance is well matched for lightweight microservices, basic web hosting, and software development testing environments.
